claims.claim: The controlled benchmark contains 24 development bases and 120 development cases, 120 test bases and 720 test cases, and a separate oracle replay verifies all 840 cases against executable registry gold.

Development uses citation-support mismatch, comparison-evidence gap, hidden failed execution, and stale persisted state; test uses claim-evidence conflict, executed-budget mismatch, repeated-run provenance gap, result-figure summary-state conflict, and unsupported-claim contract-flag state.

The partitions are exact-source-hash-disjoint and fault-family-disjoint but reuse semantically equivalent generated bases, and the two metadata-state test mutations account for 240 of 600 fault cases. The frozen suite does not bind the historical corpus-generator source at execution time; oracle replay establishes artifact consistency, not that historical identity, and exact hash disjointness does not establish held-out-source generalization or content-level figure and claim fault coverage.

The presence condition checks file presence and the advisory condition copies full-audit findings while forcing promote, so the deterministic contrasts are contract-mechanism ablations rather than comparative effectiveness; the fragment-model runs are a separate abstention sanity check, not a calibrated comparator.

On the fixed suite of 600 registered test fault cases, the fail-closed audit had zero false promotions while the presence checklist, always-promote condition, and advisory ablation promoted every fault case.
The fail-closed audit promoted all 120 generated clean controls; this is a fixed-suite regression result, not an independent clean-population estimate.

The advisory audit had blocker F1 and repair-owner accuracy of one but promoted every fault case; all 480 faulty predictions with an emitted blocking concern were promoted, so conditional concern-acceptance conflict was one.

Model prompts provide the same 96--98-character Results fragment across sibling variants, omit case-specific artifact paths, mutation labels, case IDs, gold metadata, and scored concern and repair-owner vocabularies, and retain the constant output reference paper/main.tex.

Each fragment-model trial contains 600 faulty and 120 clean predictions and blocks all 720 cases; the pooled row contains 1,800 faulty and 360 clean prediction records, with decision accuracy .5, macro-F1 .1667, blocker precision, recall, and F1 zero, repair-owner accuracy zero, and trace coverage one. These are fragment-level abstention diagnostics, not clean-utility or actionability estimates.

H1--H4 use exact observed fixed-suite values for their post-hoc threshold decisions; empirical base_bundle_id bootstrap percentile intervals are sensitivity diagnostics only, remain degenerate for uniform boundary outcomes, and are not population confidence intervals or decision bounds.

Recovery starts from fail-closed artifact-audit predictions with decision and repair-owner accuracy one and is evaluated by the same audit; it does not test erroneous routing or independent semantic validation.

Same-gate reacceptance is 120 of 120 for each of five fault families; exact clean-tree restoration is 120 of 120 for executed-budget mismatch, result-figure summary state, and unsupported-claim contract flag, and zero of 120 for claim-evidence conflict and repeated-run provenance, totaling 360 of 600 with no clean-control regression. Claim-evidence repair restores only an existing valid claim-bound evidence ID and does not invent removed citation metadata.

The manuscript-only condition completed three 720-request local runs and 2,160 predictions with distinct self-recorded output bundles; receipt distinctness is not statistical replication, and the records do not establish external provider identity, statistical independence, independently recomputable receipt preimages, or execution-time source identity.

Three earlier schema-1.0 attempt ledgers self-report stale-running recovery counts of 499, 479, and 479 responses before all three 720-request trials completed. They record observed manifest and artifact hashes but do not preserve checkpoint preimage files, independently verify their recorded prefix contents, or establish the interruption cause; current runner code requires hash-bound preimage snapshots for future stale takeovers.
